styleWhy: The story is a share and a growth rate (percentages, terawatt-hours, a doubling), so clean animated charts show the comparison better than any scene of a solar panel could.

copy.idea: Solar still makes only a small slice of the world's electricity, but it is growing faster than any other source: up 29% in a single year and doubled in three.
copy.hook: How much of the world's electricity comes from the Sun?
copy.body:
In 2024, solar made 6.9% of all the electricity the world generated: about 1 unit in every 15.

That is still small. Coal alone made about a third, and gas more than a fifth.

But solar is the speed story. Its output grew 29% in one year, adding 474 TWh, and it has doubled in just three years since 2021.

For the third year in a row, solar was the world's largest source of new electricity. Small slice, fastest growth.

facts.text: Solar generated 6.9% of global electricity in 2024 (2,131 TWh).
Shares of global electricity in 2024: coal ≈34%, gas ≈22%, hydro ≈14%, nuclear ≈9%, wind ≈8%, solar ≈7%.
Solar generation grew 29% in 2024, adding 474 TWh.
Global solar generation doubled in the three years since 2021.
Solar was the largest source of new electricity generation worldwide for the third year in a row in 2024.

shots.title: Hook: how much is solar?
shots.show: Rolling counter: a huge gold '0.0%' fills the middle of the navy frame and rolls up to 6.9%, landing with a bounce. Behind it a soft gold sun disc pulses; beneath it a thin full-width bar (the 'world electricity' bar of shot 2) fills just its first 6.9% in gold, the rest dim slate. Small label above: 'SHARE OF WORLD ELECTRICITY · 2024'.
shots.motion: Counter rolls 0→6.9 in 1.6 s and bounces; the gold sliver wipes in with it; sun disc breathes; light rays rotate slowly behind the number.

shots.title: Still a small slice
shots.show: Split bar: the same world-electricity bar from shot 1, now tall and vertical down the frame, splits into labelled segments stacking from the top: coal 34%, gas 22%, hydro 14%, nuclear 9%, wind 8%, solar 7% (gold) at the bottom, plus a thin 'other'. Fossil segments in muted slate-red, clean sources in teal, solar in gold. Each segment's % counter rolls as it appears; the coal block is outlined so its size beside solar is obvious.
shots.motion: Segments slide in one after another from the top with rolling percentages; at the end the gold solar segment glows and a bracket compares it with the coal block.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025 (shares of 2024 generation, rounded)

shots.title: +29% in one year
shots.show: Two gold vertical bars side by side: 2023 (≈1,657 TWh) and 2024 (2,131 TWh). The 2024 bar grows past the 2023 bar; the extra slice on top is highlighted bright gold with a rolling '+474 TWh' label. A big '+29%' counter rolls at the top. Ground dots stream upward into the new slice like particles of energy.
shots.motion: 2023 bar rises first, then the 2024 bar grows and overshoots; the added slice fills with flowing particles while +29% and +474 TWh roll up.

shots.title: Doubled in three years
shots.show: Shared timeline: a horizontal axis 2021 → 2024 with a cursor running along it. A gold block for 2021 output sits at the left; as the cursor moves, a copy of the block clones and stacks on top, ending as exactly two equal blocks at 2024 with a big '×2' landing beside them.
shots.motion: Cursor sweeps 2021→2024 in 2.5 s; the block grows continuously, splits into two equal halves with a snap; '×2' drops in with a bounce.

shots.title: Biggest source of new power
shots.show: Bar race: horizontal bars labelled 'New electricity added' for 2022, 2023, 2024, one row per year; in each row solar's gold bar races other sources (teal wind, slate others) and finishes first, a gold '#1' badge stamping on it. Three badges stack in a column on the right, then a '3 years running' tag.
shots.text: #1 source of new power, 3 years running
shots.motion: Rows race in turn, each about 0.9 s; gold bar overtakes and the #1 badge stamps; the three badges glow together at the end.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025 (bar lengths illustrative; ranking from source)

shots.title: End card
shots.show: The world-electricity bar from shot 1 returns, gold sliver at 6.9%, and an upward gold arrow labelled '+29%/yr' pushes the sliver wider as the title sets above: 'Small slice. Fastest growth.' Source line at the foot.
shots.motion: Gold sliver creeps wider under the arrow; title types in; sun disc glows softly behind.

recurring.name: World electricity bar
recurring.design: One long bar standing for 100% of world electricity in 2024, rounded ends, dim slate fill; solar's 6.9% always gold and always at the same end (left when horizontal, bottom segment when the bar stands vertical in shot 2); clean sources teal, fossil sources muted slate-red; label 'WORLD ELECTRICITY · 2024' in small caps.

recurring.name: Solar gold
recurring.design: Solar is always warm gold (bars, counters, badges, sun disc); other clean sources teal; fossil fuels muted slate-red; never swapped.
